hook: Critics claimed the 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image of the M87* black hole was fake.

sections.voiceover: Critics claimed the 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image of the M87* black hole was fake.
sections.visual_cue: Deep space shot of the M87* black hole glowing ring

sections.voiceover: The Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration captured this massive black hole shadow in 2019. How did researchers prove the M87* shadow is a real physical structure in space?
sections.visual_cue: Side-by-side comparison of the 2019 EHT image and raw telescope data

sections.voiceover: However, 4 CSIRO researchers used new interferometric techniques to prove the ring is real.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of the four researchers' names on a screen

sections.voiceover: Published in Nature in 2026, their independent study used a new interferometric technique to reanalyze the data. General relativity is now validated by this 2026 Nature study of the M87* shadow.
sections.visual_cue: Animation showing the interferometric data mapping onto the black hole shadow

sections.voiceover: The shadow of M87* is exactly where physics predicted.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out from the M87* black hole into the vastness of space
